featured_reviews.name: Karan Rawool
featured_reviews.review_text:
District China was one of the restaurants i had wanted to try because of their very unique and eye catching menu, so I gave it a try and it was absolutely amazing.

The things I tried:

1) Thai spiced steamed Chicken:
Marinated chicken with rock crushed herb sticks and ginger wrapped in banana leaf served with sweet chilli. Tender chicken chunks with so many different flavor combinations!
Definitely a must try for the Thai food lovers. Tasted even better with the sweet chilli. A very unique preparation too!

2)Nasi goreng:
Indonesian chicken flavored rice topped with egg. Served with Chicken satay and prawn crackers and also peanut sauce.
The rice was pretty great with a fragrant aroma. The satays were pretty great, 10pcs in total and had a sweet flavor which tasted great with the dip. Overall the combination and preparation was amazing including the prawn crackers.

Definitely recommend this place for the authentic cuisines which they offer!

featured_reviews.name: sahil mule
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hello foodies 🙋🏻‍♂️
Some day ago I ordered Chinese food from district Chinas.
I ordered:-
▪️katsu curry chicken:- Katsu curry is a very simple combination of Katsu (typically breaded pork or chicken), egg rice and curry sauce. This sauce is actually sweet, tangy, and salty at the same time.
▪️Cottage cheese BBQ bao:-
The cottage cheese was soft, bao is loaded with paneer pieces, paneer is marinated in soya sauce, and this gives you a superb test and aroma.
▪️Duet of pepper chicken:- paper Chicken it's a little bit spicy, chicken is marinated in pepper powder that's why it gives a spicy taste. The chicken is so soft and very well cooked.

All the three dishes were extremely good and delicious. The food was delivered neatly. The packing was very good, definitely ordering again from here.❣️❣️

featured_reviews.name: Shahnawaz Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Fire Bowl, Versova and had a good experience overall, though it feels a bit expensive for Chinese food. The Chicken Manchow Soup was excellent — rich, flavorful, and perfectly balanced.
Both Hakka Noodles and Hong Kong Rice were cooked very well with generous portions and great taste. Easily 5/5 for soup, noodles, and rice.
Crispy Chicken and Prawns Chilly were tasty and well-prepared, but slightly on the oily side. Service was slow and could be more attentive, especially during busy hours.Food quality is definitely good, especially soups, noodles, and rice, but pricing is on the higher side for Chinese cuisine. Worth visiting occasionally, not for regular dining.

Food is decent. Chinese cuisine is good portion size is also good.
I ordered Thai Tom Yum Soup, was unlike anything Thai I have had before. Just salt added to chicken stock. We returned it to ask them to remake it again in Thai style. When it turned up again it was the same no taste. Then i realised ordering soups is my mistake. So we were ok with the food but the over all ambience is warm. I was served Thai Soup with a stainless steel cutlery dinner spoon which they call a soup spoon. When I asked them are you serving soup or chicken shorba they said in premium AC seating we serve in stainless steel only. So was amazed at his answer and didn’t have any reaction. They could use some nice bone chine soup
Spoons or Ceramic Soup Spoons in thier AC Seating. When you charge customers you should also be able to serve with the same amount of courtesy & detail.

Best of Luck to the guys need to get the game right. AC or Non AC end of the kitchen where the food is made is the same and that’s the soul of your restaurant.

There used to be a time when fire Bowl was our goto place for any celebration or when we yearned for comfort Chinese food... Their food was good, prices were at the upper side but still reasonable for the quality provided...

Not anymore... Their prices have rose astronomically but the quality and taste has gone down.... The delivery takes a lot of time... So overall not worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dining at Baoji has, over the years, become more than just a meal for us—it’s a cherished ritual and a celebration of Pan-Asian excellence. Chef Kapil’s menu is nothing short of extraordinary—an immersive gastronomic journey across Asia where every dish is crafted with finesse, depth, and bold, unforgettable flavours. From the fragrant warmth of Thai curries to the delicate precision of Japanese classics, each plate feels thoughtfully curated and beautifully executed.

Over the years, we’ve explored almost every vegetarian and non-vegetarian offering on the menu, and the consistency is remarkable. Our all-time favourites include the Prawns Tempura Sushi, Spicy Crispy Prawns Cheung Fun, KRA Paw Rice, and the Spicy Teriyaki Chicken with Japanese sushi rice. The Chicken Katsu Donburi Rice is comforting and deeply satisfying, while the Baoji Style Sizzled Chilli Chicken is fiery, aromatic, and perfectly balanced.

The Purple Chicken Bao remains one of our absolute favourites—soft, pillowy, and bursting with flavour. The Chicken and Scallop Siu, Crab Meat Spicy Dumplings, and Sichuan Tiger Prawns are standout dishes that elevate the experience further. The Miso Ramen Bowl (chicken) and Pad Thai Noodles are soulful and generous, while the Japanese Tebasaki Chicken is addictive. The New Zealand Lamb Chops, whether in black pepper sauce or mixed berry teriyaki glaze, are succulent and refined.

One dish that truly steals the show is the banana-wrapped fish with sticky rice—the gravy, the fragrant rice, and the perfectly steamed fish wrapped in banana leaf come together in a spectacular, unforgettable combination.

They also boast a commendable selection of sashimi and nigiri, along with excellent soups and salads that complement the meal beautifully.

What truly completes the experience is the warm, humble hospitality of the staff. It has been many years of being regulars here, and Baoji remains our favourite monthly ritual. This isn’t just dining—it’s a celebration of flavours, craftsmanship, and heartfelt service.

I had the misfortune of dining at The Grand Asian cuisine , and let me just say, this was an experience I'd rather forget. The name should have been a warning, but I foolishly ignored it.

The first red flag was the smell when I walked in—a rancid blend of burnt oil and something that could only be described as old gym socks. The decor looked like it hadn't been updated since the 70s, and not in a charming, retro way—more like they just never bothered.

I ordered the "special of the day," which was a mistake I'll regret forever. The steak was so overcooked it could have doubled as a hockey puck. It was dry, tasteless, and somehow both burnt and raw at the same time. The mashed potatoes on the side had the consistency of paste and the flavor of cardboard. The vegetables were a sad, mushy mess, as if they’d been boiled into oblivion.

And don't even get me started on the service. The waiter seemed more interested in his phone than in actually serving customers. When he did acknowledge my existence, it was with a look that said he had better things to do.

To top it all off, I ended the night with a stomach ache that left me questioning every decision that led me to this point. If you’re considering eating here, do yourself a favor and go literally anywhere else. Your stomach and taste buds will thank you.

That should capture the essence of a terrible food experience!

featured_reviews.name: Kartik Pujary
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently dined at Chowman in Andheri West, and the experience truly lived up to the brand’s reputation for authentic and flavourful Chinese cuisine. From the moment you step in, the ambience feels warm and refined, with comfortable seating and a calm, classy vibe that works equally well for family meals and casual dining.

We ordered a mix of starters and mains, and every dish was well-presented and packed with flavour. The Kung Pao Veg (Dry) was perfectly balanced—crispy, spicy, and not overly oily. The Crispy Chilli Baby Corn stood out with its crunch and bold seasoning, making it an excellent starter. The Coriander Burnt Garlic Veg Rice was aromatic and light, with generous portions and a nice balance of vegetables, while the Chilli Garlic Baby Corn & Mushroom gravy complemented the rice beautifully with its rich, tangy sauce and fresh ingredients.

Portion sizes are generous, making the meal great value for money. Service was prompt and courteous—the staff was attentive without being intrusive, and orders arrived well-timed. Cleanliness, presentation, and overall attention to detail were clearly noticeable, right down to the neat table setup and menu presentation.

The bill was reasonable for the quality and quantity served, and everything felt fairly priced. Chowman Andheri West is a reliable spot if you’re craving authentic Indo-Chinese and Chinese flavours done right. I would definitely recommend it and look forward to visiting again to explore more from their extensive menu. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

featured_reviews.name: Shaikh Khalid Sarfaraz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Chowman is located in Andheri West and it is near the Andheri Sports Complex and on the main road hence easy to find.

This brand hails from Kolkata and they have their presence in multiple cities. This particular outlet has indoor and outdoor seatings available and they have used the space nicely. The decor is decent and the overall vibe of the restaurant is nice.

The menu here is one of the best as they have covered a lot of items. The variety available is amazing and pricing is not high. The quantity and quality of whatever we tried was excellent. They also have a kids menu plus they run various offers too.

We went here for dinner and the kitchen service was on time. Special thanks to Staff Dhiraj & Santanu as they knew the menu well and they were attentive and proactive.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Doremon’s Beloved Red Chicken -
From the kids menu. This was honey sesame chicken. Taste wise good however too crispy hence hard and chewy. Need improvement.

Smokey Chicken -
Chicken tossed in garlic chilli based sauce tasted really good. Loved the juicy chicken and the smokey flavours of the chilli was good plus the garlic didn’t had strong taste.

Kolkata Style Chilli Shrimp -
One of the best shrimp dish. Tossed in soy sauce again not with overpowering flavours this dish was tasted really good. The fresh prawns, the crunchy outer layer and the sauce was this dish excellent.

MAINS~
Pan Fried Noodles -
Again one of the best pan fired noodles experience. Lightly fried noodled with soy based gravy, veggies, chicken and prawns. Trust me this is a must try as it tasted outstanding.

Chowman’s Special Rice with Hong Kong Chicken Gravy -
Rice with egg, chicken and prawns paired with hot Hong Kong gravy was soul satisfying. Loved the combination and taste wise both the dishes were excellent.

DESSERT~
Chocolate Mousse -
The mousse was chocolatey and creamy plus it was fresh and wasn’t too sweet. Hence tasted delicious.

BEVERAGES~
Thai Lemonade.
Sparkling Blueberry.
Both the drinks tasted nice and paired nicely with the food.

So our meal at Chowman Andheri West was one of the best Chinese food experiences I’ve had. They also run dine in offers so do check that before going. Highly recommended and a must try.

Taking you through all the food items that we tried

Chowman’s Special Rice

Their in-house special Fried Rice consisting of exotic vegetables, shrimps, chicken & wrapped up with egg. Quite flavourful.

Pan Fried Noodles

Noodles pan fried and served with chicken, veggies in a thick gravy.

Brownie

This brownie was served with vanilla ice cream and chocolate sauce poured over it.

For mocktails, we tried the Thai Lemonade, Sizzling Blueberry and Tangy Pineapple, which were quite refreshing.

Overall, the food was really decent. They have both indoor as well as outdoor seating. This place is famous for their sea food so if you love fish/prawns, then it’s a heaven for you. They also have a large vegetarian section in the menu. Really impressed with the taste.

Walking into Chin Chin Chu is like stepping into a high-fashion graphic novel. The design language is a playful nod to Chinoiserie, but through a filter of modern pop art.

The Liquid Art – Mixology at its Finest
Before the first plate arrives, one must navigate the drink menu. The bar at Chin Chin Chu is not an afterthought; it is a destination in itself.
The Signature Cocktails: I started with the "K-Pop," a vodka-based concoction infused with hibiscus and a hint of spice. It was refreshing, visually stunning, and packed a subtle punch. For those who prefer something more grounded, their Wasabi Martini offers a clean, nasal-clearing sharpness that perfectly prepares the palate for raw fish.
The Non-Alcoholic Game: Their mocktails—often overlooked in other establishments—are complex. The "Asian Spice Trail" with star anise and kaffir lime was so well-balanced I didn't even miss the spirit.

featured_reviews.name: Vedant lad
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dropped by this gem the other day we were at Juhu beach and this one is cited at a walk of 5 mins from the Novotel end. Talking about the ambience first, they have indoor as well as outdoor dining area. The entire space looks extremely vibrant and full of colours which looks absolutely beautiful. Coming to the f&b, for our first round of drinks we ordered for Kung Fu Panda which was a gin-based cocktail having refreshing elements like Basil, lemongrass ginger, star anise and passionfruit. Loved the way it was presented which made it totally gramworthy. Next, we had Golden dynasty from their Chinese new years menu, this one was vodka base and had lovely taste as it had citrusy elements. The food menu here is wide spread and offers almost everything you could think of. We tried their Philadelphia Cream cheese and miso Dimsums and hands down these are one of the finest cheese dimsums we have tried in a while. Next we had Crab Salad and tempura prawn sushi which also had cream cheese drizzled on top of it. Mild and mellow flavour profile yet the chef managed to make it so delectable. This one was so good that we had to repeat it. Upon or servers recommendation, we tried Prawns in butter garlic which was wok tossed prawns drenched in butter garlic sauce. Simple and perfect which can't go wrong. Later for the mains, we tried Exotic Mushroom clay pot rice which was topped with truffle butter sauce. The pot rice had a generous amount of veggies and especially mushrooms. We lastly ordered for Chilli garlic noodles which were thin noodles wok tossed in chilli garlic sauce along with chicken - this was totally worth every penny. Now for round two of drinks we tried chin chin gin and Oogway’s paloma which was again gin base cocktail. Both the cocktails were a solid 10.
For dessert, we had Nutella wellcake which was soft and gooey cake drenched in Nutella. Overall it was a lovely dining experience and we will be coming here again for sure.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had high expectations for this restaurant, but it turned out to be a major letdown. We ordered chicken manchow soup and chicken lollipop, and both dishes were unacceptable.

The soup arrived with chicken that wasn't fresh and had a foul smell. After we complained, they replaced it, but the damage was done. The chicken lollipop was even worse – we found a feather on our first bite. When we showed it to the waiter, he promised to replace it, but instead brought back the same lollipop that had clearly just been double-fried.

The lack of food quality and kitchen hygiene is alarming. I cannot recommend this place and won't be returning

featured_reviews.name: Ap Consultants
featured_reviews.review_text:
While this Juhu chinese street stall comes highly recommended, it unfortunately didn't live up to the hype.
The food quality is indistinguishable from any average roadside stall, yet the pricing is on par with full-service restaurants. Between the lack of hygiene and the premium price tag for a 'no-frills' experience.
It simply doesn't offer good value for money.

featured_reviews.name: Emeline Dias
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst worst they should give us a refund for serving this kind of food worst.

One of the most disappointing Chinese food experiences I’ve had. The Burnt Garlic Fried Rice was extremely oily, and the Masala Lollipop was undercooked and tasted like it had been poorly defrosted and served. This place is so hyped that they’ve forgotten the most important thing serving good food. Definitely did not live up to the reputation. Would not recommend.

featured_reviews.name: Harshada Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a horrible experience here and would not recommend it to anyone. We started with the Manchow soup, which was pathetic—the chicken was actually stinking. While the staff replaced it, the second bowl tasted just as bad as the first.
The biggest disappointment was the Chicken Lollipop. It’s my favorite dish, but we found chicken feathers still on the meat. When we pointed this out, the staff took the plate away and simply double-fried the same pieces before bringing them back out. We couldn't believe the lack of hygiene and basic service. We left the food on the table and walked out.

featured_reviews.name: Rahil Kotadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of desi Chinese, this roadside gem in Juhu is definitely worth checking out. It’s run by the same people behind Sagar Chinese House, the popular seating restaurant located near Juhu PVR. Together, they’ve earned quite a name for serving some of the best Indo-Chinese food in the Juhu–Andheri belt.

The food here packs bold flavours and generous portions — truly great value for money when you compare the quality and quantity. Their Manchow Soup, Chicken Crispy, and Triple Rice are absolute must-tries — each dish has that perfect street-style punch that keeps you coming back for more.

That said, the service is a real weak spot. It’s slow and needs serious improvement. A bit more attention to service would easily make this place a complete winner.

featured_reviews.name: Aditya Pandit
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went there with a friend of mine today after watching a video online and I’ll be very clear with you guys the place is not worth the hype. Please don’t come here and spend your precious time on this.
We ordered 3 items Veg burnt garlic rice and Manchurian gravy (Kartik Aryan’s fav) and Schezwan noodles. All of them tasted so bad we were not able to eat it after a few bites. It was so bad I’ll not even feed that to my own dog. We ended up taking it away because throwing it away in front of them would have been disrespectful.
And now the best part we asked him for our bill he says 890. Money is not the issue here taste and quality is. Homemade Maggi tastes better than that. If it was tasty I would have had no problem but it was not edible. I’ll advise everyone to not come here. Rest it’s up to you if you want to come and experience what I said in the review in person.
